capabilities: Arrange files and folders by hand with drag-and-drop, cut, and paste
Switch the file pane between four two-pane and drill layouts
Create pages from folder-level templates with date, name, and rollover tokens
Search the whole vault by word prefix with highlighted in-note results
Hide folders and attachment files from the tree and color sections
disambiguation: Not just a manual-sorting plugin; it also restructures the explorer into two-pane layouts and adds page templates and vault-wide search.
extras: The README includes a disclosure of what the community catalog's capability scan reports (vault enumeration and clipboard write), states the plugin makes no network requests, and warns to disable competing sorting plugins (Manual Sorting, Custom File Explorer sorting, Bartender).
motivation: The README says other manual-sort plugins hook the explorer's DOM with observers and per-item listeners and slow down past 10,000 notes, so the author built one that hooks the sort itself to stay fast.
problem: Obsidian's file explorer sorts only by its built-in orders and offers no manual arrangement, two-pane browsing, or fast word-prefix search across a large vault.

relations.evidence: turn on Search image text and install Power Extract, and the words inside your images become searchable
with Power Assistant installed, a chip in the search box answers questions from your own notes

summary: File explorer overhaul that adds manual drag-and-drop ordering, two-pane folder layouts, page templates, and instant prefix search across the vault.
